gamespot.com/articles/15-things-you-need.title: 15 Things You Need To Know Before You Play The Blood Of Dawnwalker
gamespot.com/articles/15-things-you-need.excerpt: Are you looking for The Blood of Dawnwalker tips? This is an open-world RPG made by the talented folks who, once upon a time, helped with the development of The Witcher 3. You can expect everything from macabre creatures and dark fantasy themes, as well as unique mechanics that are totally refreshing for the genre. Of course, it goes without saying that things can get a tad bit confusing at first, which is why our guide aims to assist you for the long road ahead. You’re a Dawnwalker - A part-human, part-vampire hybrid In The Blood of Dawnwalker, you play as Coen, a commoner from a small village called Laslea Glen. Circumstances have not only caused Coen’s family to get kidnapped by vampire lords known as vrakhiri. He’s also been turned into a monstrosity--a dawnwalker--someone who lives as a human by day and turns into a vampire at night. This dynamic changes how you approach the game. During the day, you heal up normally by eating food and you chat with shopkeepers who ply their craft in settlements. You may also cast Witchcraft spells and commune with the spirits of the dead. You’re basically a warrior-spellcaster with the limitations of being human. Just a medieval warrior hunting for wolves. Learn to manage your bloodthirst as a vampire Things change drastically at night. As a vampire, you need to satisfy your bloodthirst. This means feeding on hapless stragglers and wildlife. If your health is too low and you approach a person, you might lose control, causing you to bleed them dry as you feast. That said, being a lord of the night has its perks. You get to use serrated claws to strike foes. You get to teleport across short distances. And, yes, you can even walk vertically on walls, defying gravity and all that is holy. Related guide: How to heal as a vampire Drink the blood of your enemies (left), and be ready if you're about to lose control (right). gamespot.com/articles/you-can-give-up-in.title: You Can Give Up In The Blood Of Dawnwalker And Leave Vale Sangora For Good
gamespot.com/articles/you-can-give-up-in.excerpt: Most video games encourage you to keep trying. Even when all seems lost or when a challenge feels insurmountable, every failure is just part of the learning curve. But The Blood of Dawnwalker , from developer Rebel Wolves and publisher Bandai Namco, eschews that age-old mantra. Instead, it has a joke ending where you simply give up on the campaign and leave the game world forever. In This Article How to leave Vale Sangora in The Blood of Dawnwalker Crossing the chasm From hero to zero How to leave Vale Sangora in The Blood of Dawnwalker You can leave Vale Sangora in The Blood of Dawnwalker as soon as you’re done with the prologue. When you’re ready, simply make your way from Laslea Glen to the western edge of the map. Just past the woods in Briar Sloughs, you’ll see an aptly named Shrine called the Coward’s Path. Travel along the road and you’ll stumble upon a side quest known as The Cursed Chasm. There, you’ll spot a broken bridge and a ravine. If you look across the gap, you’ll notice that the road continues all the way to a large gate that hasn’t been blockaded yet. A map showing the location of the exit gate. Crossing the chasm To get this joke ending in The Blood of Dawnwalker, you have to reach the gate at the end of the path. But, before you could do that, you have to get across the chasm first: Make sure it’s nighttime so that Coen turns into a vampire. Jump across and spam the Shadowstep button so you can latch on a rock at the opposite side. Then, with a combination of Planeshift and Shadowstep, climb to the other side of the ravine. When you approach the gate, pick [Leave the valley forever]. Cross the ravine (left) and escape the valley (right). From hero to zero Coen will admit that he has to find a new home and make a new life for himself. He won’t rescue his family anymore and he’ll leave the rest of the region under the rule of the vampire boyars. gamespot.com/articles/blood-of-dawnwalke.excerpt: Are you planning to sell silver in The Blood of Dawnwalker ? With Vale Sangora under the rule of vampire lords, it’s no wonder that the sale of silver has been banned. Those who break the law are swiftly executed. In This Article Selling silver in The Blood of Dawnwalker Silver trader location Silver trader wares Selling silver in The Blood of Dawnwalker You’ll find all sorts of silver items while exploring the game world. Some are inside chests that you loot, while others are placed on shelves and tables, easy enough to steal when no one’s looking. Examples include bowls, crosses, chalices, jewelry, dining utensils, and even lumps of silver ore. Items made of silver net you a lot of cash. Silver trader location To sell silver in The Blood of Dawnwalker, you need to head to Svartrau City in the middle of the world map. Make your way to the southwestern part of the fortified settlement and look for the path that leads to Neustadt. Just past a couple of guards, you should spot a building. Go through the door and have a chat with the vendor. Svartrau City (left) has a vendor who's willing to buy your silver items (right). Silver trader wares You can part with all your silver goods in exchange for more denarii. Oh, and don’t forget to check the vendor’s wares. In our playthrough, this fella had three legendary items up for grabs: Legendary weapon: The Kingslayer Legendary amulet: Fear of the Wilds Legendary ring: Slicer’s Ring Note: If you want to get more cash when selling items, be sure to level up the Bewitching Influence perk in the Witchcraft tree. At level 2, it increases all selling prices by +15%. That does it for our guide on where to sell your silver in The Blood of Dawnwalker. We’re hoping that you can amass a ton of cash, enough to upgrade various weapons and armors, as well as purchase items that allow you to heal as a vampire .

How to get the ingredients from Anca You can find Anca in the southeastern part of Laslea Glen. Meet up with her by the river, then chat with her inside her hut. Pay Anca 50 denarii to buy the items. “I really have to go” - This costs 1x Time Segment. Coen leaves with the items. “Gladly. I’ve missed it too” - This costs 2x Time Segment instead. It leads to a short but sweet moment where Coen bonds with Anca. It’s worth seeing if you plan on romancing Anca later on. Anca has the ingredients you need. How to make the correct brew Of course, you still need to brew the potion if you want to save Coen’s mom in The Blood of Dawnwalker: This process costs 1x Time Segment. Before reentering your home, read the Instructions From Anca in your inventory. After the cutscene where Coen starts making the brew, pick “use hot water.” Followed by “three scoops.” Coen will feed Esme the stew, which contains the medicine. rockpapershotgun.com/i-just-want-to-go-b.excerpt: As I stand on the lee side of the wrecked haz lab, all I can hear is the rain pelt its metal roof and the feral wind howl about me. Planet LV-921 may have a breathable atmosphere, but it's not a safe planet. rockpapershotgun.com/in-dungeon-settlers.title: In Dungeon Settlers, you build a colony on top of a teeming RPG labyrinth in a trim take on Rimworld
rockpapershotgun.com/in-dungeon-settlers.excerpt: The first time I lost my whole party in Dungeon Settlers, it was to a swarm of rats. I think we can all agree that getting killed by rats in anything remotely fantasy RPG-ish is an enormous faux pas. It's like spelling your own name wrong on your CV. It's like accidentally wearing your underpants on top of your trousers. It's like failing to become Thane of Whiterun. In my defence, I was playing the game on Hard difficulty, and the rodents of Dungeon Settlers have a zoologically improbable habit of keeping company with stone golems. Ever tried to crack a stone golem with a wooden sword? I have found it inconvenient. In any case, while my party wipe was embarrassing, it was also excellently macabre in the fine traditions of Dwarf Fortress . Read more

gamespot.com/articles/final-fantasy-vii-.excerpt: Final Fantasy VII Revelation finally has a release date: April 8, 2027. Square Enix confirmed the news today during the PlayStation State of Play livestream , along with nearly 10 minutes of new footage. The release date was confirmed via a trailer highlights all eight playable characters in the main party: Cloud, Tifa, Barret, Red XIII, Yuffie, Cait Sith, Vincent, and Cid. We also see gameplay of the team in action, including team-up abilities like Vincent's Galian Beast form rushing a group of enemies with Red XIII, and Tifa and Yuffie attacking from above with a dive kick/spinning shuriken combo. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8YHP48v7vyg From there, FF7 director Naoki Hamaguchi introduced an extended look at raw gameplay, which focused on traveling the massive world map. Invoking the original game's PlayStation 1 roots, the Highwind flies over the world of Gaia, and players can pilot it wherever they wish. Once they reach a location of interest, they can choose a party from any of the eight playable characters, and then parachute down to the surface instantly. The demo then dives into a side quest in Gongaga featuring Sotetsu, a character featured in a FF7 Rebirth side quest. Yuffie, knowing Sotetsu from that side quest, has a special interaction with him, implying that some missions may play out differently depending on the characters brought to complete them. Along with the news of Final Fantasy VII Revelation's April 8 release date, the Steam page for the game dropped a few hints on what is coming after launch, with listings for story expansions featuring two key characters .

gamespot.com/articles/final-fantasy-reso.title: Final Fantasy Resonance Is A Return To Classic Series Conventions While Also Evolving Square Enix’s HD-2D Style
gamespot.com/articles/final-fantasy-reso.excerpt: Given its rich legacy spanning almost four decades, it's something of a surprise that Square Enix has taken its time to give Final Fantasy an outing in HD-2D, the retro-modern aesthetic that clearly harks back to the pinnacle of pixel art from RPG classics of the 16-bit era, including Final Fantasy VI. But rather than introduce this visual style to the franchise with a brand-new title, Square Enix is using the HD-2D treatment to reimagine and preserve a now-defunct mobile game. Final Fantasy Resonance is a reimagining of Final Fantasy Brave Exvius that's similar in scope to Octopath Traveler 0, an enhanced console adaptation for Octopath Traveler: Champions of the Continent. Although Final Fantasy Resonance is a retelling of Brave Exvius's first season, casting you in the role of Rain along with party members Lasswell, Fina, and Lid, the mobile title was played with just touch controls, and so there's naturally been an overhaul to the control system to suit a console experience. But from hands-on at Gamescom 2026 plenty more has been overhauled and added to transform this from the mobile game's streamlined structure and limited exploration into something you would expect from a classic Final Fantasy title that can be enjoyed at a leisurely pace, including traversing an overworld map, where you can also summon a chocobo for getting around. At a glance, the turn-based battle system shares some similarities with Octopath Traveler, with a timeline at the top showing the order of party members and enemies' turns, as well as a stagger system, albeit not like that series' puzzle of chipping away at enemy weaknesses. But being a Final Fantasy game, it has many of the series' classic tropes too. gamespot.com/articles/epic-games-new-voi.title: Epic Games’ New Voice Chat Lets You Keep Talking To Friends While Playing Different Games
gamespot.com/articles/epic-games-new-voi.excerpt: Epic Games has announced that it's going to make it easier than ever to hang out and talk with friends across different platforms by launching Epic Parties. This voice chat service will work across Fortnite (on all supported platforms), the Epic Games Store launcher (PC, iOS, and Android), and the Epic Games app (iOS and Android). For example, you can start a voice party from your phone or PC launcher, ring up a friend who is busy playing Fortnite on their PlayStation, and even transfer that call from your phone to your PC when you get back to your desk. This means that you can sit in on a voice call through the Epic PC Launcher while playing completely different games from your Epic library. Other benefits include a seamless approach to grouping friends together, as Epic says that if you're in a voice party with friends and everyone decides to open Fortnite, then the game will automatically drop you all into the same lobby together. This new feature is competing directly with Discord, which has been the go-to third-party app for users for several years. Epic's built-in alternative aims to let users bring their social list, voice channels, and digital avatar with them across multiple platforms and from game to game, whether you are on iOS, Android, PC, or console. Epic has also hinted that these voice and avatar systems will be integrated directly into Unreal Engine 6, and the tools will be offered to other developers in time. For now, it's currently rolling out to Fortnite, and Epic Parties will be available in Rocket League next year. According to Epic's year-in-review stats , over $1 billion was spent in the store in 2025, and it reached an all-time record of 78 million monthly active users on PC. Earlier this year, Epic spoke more about its plans to further improve its digital storefront . gamespot.com/articles/gta-6-limited-edit.excerpt: During today's State of Play broadcast, Sony announced that two limited-edition Grand Theft Auto 6 -themed DualSense controllers will be released. Elsewhere, the GTA 6 logo is etched on to the touchpad, and palm-tree-like shapes are embossed on the controller grips. Both controls launch alongside GTA 6 on its release date, November 19. Surely there's no better way to experience the biggest gaming release of the decade so far? They'll set you back $85 each. gamespot.com/articles/gta-6-fishing-and-.title: GTA 6 Fishing And Hunting Doesn’t Work Like You Think It Does
gamespot.com/articles/gta-6-fishing-and-.excerpt: Rockstar Games has confirmed new details about how fishing and hunting work in GTA 6, and it's probably not what you would expect. Speaking to YouTuber TGG , Rockstar North's Rob Nelson confirmed that fishing in GTA 6 is limited to catch and release--players cannot keep any fish. Why? "It didn't fit this game," Nelson said, adding that fishing in GTA 6 is mainly for fun. Players can also complete fishing-related challenges and amass collectibles. Jason fishing in GTA 6. In Rockstar's last game, 2018's Red Dead Redemption II, players could catch a great assortment of fish and then cook and eat them. That made sense given the time period of the game, that being 1899. GTA 6 is set in modern times, and main characters Jason and Lucia, like you and me, have access to numerous food options at any given time. Eating food in GTA 6 will make you gain weight, and players can use the excess calories to bulk up at the gym. As for hunting in GTA 6, Nelson said the game's hunting system is one of many ways in the game that players can make money . The hunting system is unlocked through a friend that knows Jason, but TGG theorized that this person has not been shown yet in any GTA 6 footage so far. In addition to catching fish and killing animals, players will be able to "inspect" the creatures, borrowing a system from Red Dead Redemption 2. GTA 6 also has dogs that you can pet, scold (you monster), and inspect . GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. At the State of Play event on September 3, Sony and Rockstar announced a GTA 6-themed DualSense controller .

gamespot.com/articles/metro-2039-kicks-o.title: Metro 2039 Kicks Off A Busy February Full Of Video Game Launches
gamespot.com/articles/metro-2039-kicks-o.excerpt: During today's State of Play , 4A Games revealed new PS5 Pro footage of Metro 2039 and finally confirmed the game's release date. Narrowing down from a previously known February 2027 release window, it's now confirmed that the game will be out on February 4 of next year. That means it's currently the first high-profile AAA game launch in a month that will be full of them. In the weeks after Metro 2039's launch, we can expect the likes of Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis, God of War Laufey, Persona 4 Revival, and Fable to all come out. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rxfWaSg_-hc The new gameplay footage looked great, which makes me thankful that Metro 2039 is arriving before all those other titles. The three-minute State of Play trailer begins with The Stranger slowly exploring the remnants of a dentist's office. He discovers that some Novoreich forces are there in the apartments above, and a shootout ensues. The YouTube video description for the trailer reveals that this footage is meant to highlight the "environmental detail, kinetic combat, and the technological advances that have been made" for this new Metro game. The video description also reveals why the footage looks so good: It was captured on PS5 Pro, on which Metro 2039 has a 60fps performance mode that supports ray tracing at a 4K resolution. That performance mode will even be available on the base PS5 and Xbox Series X models, with 4A Games touting that Metro 2039 is "the first game in the series to be built from the ground up for ray tracing." gamespot.com/articles/jin-sakai-returns-.title: Jin Sakai Returns In Upcoming Ghost Of Yotei Roguelike DLC
gamespot.com/articles/jin-sakai-returns-.excerpt: Today, during the PlayStation State of Play livestream , Sucker Punch offered a look at Ghost of Yotei's upcoming roguelike mode, Most Wanted. The mode will feature four playable characters, and Yotei's Atsu, Oyuki, and Nagato will be joined by a familar face from the past: The Ghost of Tsushima, Jin Sakai, will officially return. Most Wanted, which the trailer calls a "combat survival mode," lets players choose one of the four samurai, each with their own weapons and abilities, to take them on a hunt for one of the Yotei Six. Each of the Six, if defeated, will offer a reward of coins that can then be spent to upgrade the samurai for future runs. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Nlchabfwy_w A new post on the official PlayStation Blog further explores the new mode, saying that the core of the mode lies in its Perks system. "As you progress through a run, you’ll frequently select between new perks including weapon mastery, gear loadouts, summons, parries, survivability, and more," the blog says. "These are the cornerstone of crafting the perfect build and lead to some of the most exciting surprises as you find the challenge or unexpected value that comes from mixing and matching perks. This new mode marks the first time Jin Sakai returns as a playable characters since his starring role in 2020's Ghost of Tsushima. The PS Blog post says that the development team made sure to "take his Ghost of Tsushima model and keep it faithful while also applying upgrades for Ghost of Yōtei," as he can use all four of his fighting stances from Ghost of Tsushima, as well as sticky bombs, the Dance of Wrath, and his Ghost stance. Ghost of Yotei's Echoes of Sekigahara expansion, as well as the Most Wanted roguelike mode, launch October 1. Players who own the base game can purchase a Complete Edition upgrade with the extra content, while new players can purchase Ghost of Yotei: Complete Edition with all content in one package.

gamespot.com/articles/resident-evil-trai.title: Resident Evil Trailer Shows The Sequence Where Its Star Almost Died For Real
gamespot.com/articles/resident-evil-trai.excerpt: During the September 3 State of Play , Sony debuted a new clip from the upcoming Resident Evil movie, and it was both dark and hilarious. That should be no surprise, as comedy and horror are naturally intertwined, and the movie is written and directed by sketch comedy veteran Zach Cregger. In the clip, we see Austin Abrams' character, the medical courier Bryan, running down a street in Raccoon City as zombies throw themselves off rooftops trying to catch him. They explode on impact, with blood flying everywhere. Bryan screams as he runs down the street amidst the carnage, uttering some hilarious noises and guttural screams. Check out the new footage below. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KGlapnJFacE Cregger wanted to film this sequence practically instead of using CGI. The production team created 150-pound “body-sized blood bags” that were dropped from cranes to create the effect. One of the blood bags came close to striking Abrams, and Cregger said, “It would’ve killed him.” Bryan, according to Cregger, is an "idiot" who finds himself in a horrifying situation and is just trying to survive. The entire movie feels like “one gigantic sequence,” Cregger said, adding that things begin to “pop off” five minutes into the movie–and it only ramps up from there. “It feels like one gigantic sequence,” he says. “Things pop off about five minutes in and it basically stays like that until the end. What I love about the games is that you move from set-piece to set-piece. Every location has a unique challenge. So again, I’m borrowing from the games directly in that rhythm, where you’re just running through a gauntlet.” The Resident Evil movie releases on September 18, and it's expected to have the biggest opening ever for a Resident Evil movie .

gamespot.com/articles/anime-gta-style-ga.title: Anime GTA-Style Game Ananta’s Massive Open World Could Be Its Greatest Strength Or Its Biggest Problem
gamespot.com/articles/anime-gta-style-ga.excerpt: If you're anything like me, seeing the announcement of another anime-style open-world game back in 2023 raised an eyebrow. There are so many games in a similar vein that I glance at, think look cool, and then don't find quite appealing enough to actually get me to sink time into them. Ananta had me looking twice, though. Ananta features multiple vehicles, engaging storyline missions, a roster of appealing characters, and a vast open world, meaning it's regularly referred to as "anime GTA." While my hands-on time with Naked Rain's free-to-play urban RPG at Gamescom 2026 was enjoyable, I'm still left a little confused about how the final game will look when it's released in 2027. To begin with, the story mission I played and the open world I engaged with were marked as two completely separate modes in the menu, although Rain, the game's international marketing lead, assured me that this would not be the case when Ananta is released. Ananta has two distinct cities. While Ananta clearly falls into many of the traps of a modern open-world RPG, its eccentric characters, obsession with social media, and ability to live different lives across its regions set it apart from others in the genre. But it's all just a little bit ... strange. You'll play initially as the Captain of the Countermeasures Bureau, an organization that has fallen into disrepair. Instead of rebuilding it through various tasks and heroic deeds though, the Captain decides to become an online celebrity. You'll grow your following and use that popularity to bring the Bureau back to life (obviously). Ananta even hands various cutesy nicknames to you along the way via other characters, turning the Captain's adventures into viral moments that could actually make sense in a world where everyone is permanently attached to their phone. gamespot.com/articles/mmos-have-stagnate.title: MMOs Have “Stagnated,” Guild Wars 3 Studio Head Says
gamespot.com/articles/mmos-have-stagnate.excerpt: Guild Wars 3 developer ArenaNet wants to try "wild, crazy ideas" in a genre that, according to its studio head, has "stagnated" in recent years. During a hands-off demo where early Guild Wars 3 gameplay was shown to members of the press, I asked ArenaNet studio head Colin Johanson about the state of the MMO genre in 2026 and what problems Guild Wars 3 is looking to solve. He had plenty to say on the subject. Many MMO players are still playing the same games they were 10-20 years ago, Johanson said, citing decade-old (or older) examples like World of Warcraft, The Elder Scrolls Online, Final Fantasy 14, and, of course, ArenaNet's own Guild Wars 2. In that same time, "minute-to-minute gameplay in MMOs has stagnated," even as other genres have modernized and become more approachable, he said. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ITPzxITngqA That's "really good timing" for ArenaNet and Guild Wars 3, Johanson said, and one that presents a big opportunity for a new game to break in and shake up the scene. "There's been very little new in the last decade, and a lot of those [newer] games either don't exist anymore or were canceled in development before they made their way out," Johanson said. "We see MMO fans constantly clamoring for and asking for something new and saying this genre desperately needs something new to move it forward right now." Johanson certainly has a point. The biggest new MMOs of the last few years have been games like 2021's New World or Korean MMOs like Lost Ark and Throne and Liberty , all originally tied to Amazon's game publishing arm. If nothing else, their launches showed how hungry MMO players are for a big new game in the space, with each title attracting hundreds of thousands of concurrent players in their first weeks, or in the case of Lost Ark, over 1.3 million . rockpapershotgun.com/a-game-for-everyone.title: "A game for everyone is a game for no one": Don't expect an easy ride in Carcass Clad, the co-op tank horror game from the makers of Mouthwashing
rockpapershotgun.com/a-game-for-everyone.excerpt: On my final day of Gamescom, strolling (running) around the indie area to make sure I don't miss anything good, I stumble upon Wrong Organ’s upcoming Carcass Clad. Set in a wartorn Soviet city, empty of people but littered with tanks wearing coats of Frankensteined cattle corpses (light stuff!), Carcass Clad is a three-player co-op experience that shares the stressful responsibility of piloting a tank and taking down enemy units between those unlucky three. If you read the name Wrong Organ and thought, ‘Wait, the Mouthwashing team? They're making a multiplayer co-op game?’, I can't fault your surprise. Edwin did interview them about it back in June , but I walked up to the booth knowing the devs themselves and little more, so I was experiencing all of Carcass Clad and its heavy departure from their previous work for the first time. gamespot.com/articles/dungeons-and-drago.title: Dungeons And Dragons Icons Could Take The TTRPG To A Modern-Day Setting
gamespot.com/articles/dungeons-and-drago.excerpt: The D&D Icons initiative , led by actor and longtime D&D fanatic Joe Manganiello, brings today's Dungeons & Dragons game together with famous series creators of the past, like author R.A. Salvatore's The Legend of Drizzt. But things aren't going to be strictly limited to classic fantasy settings, Manganiello has teased. Speaking to GameSpot's Jessica Cogswell at Gen Con 2026, Manganiello stressed that modern-day settings could be part of the Icons program, too. "There [are] also lots of other things that I want for Icons in the future," he said. "I think that there's a great present-day game that pushes genetics and military. We're moving at such a rapid pace, but I think there could be a game that takes place in our modern world. There are also some other worlds of D&D that I think could be revisited in new and exciting ways that weren't maximized their first time around." Manganiello, whose official title is chief creative officer, is keeping specifics secret for now, but it sounds like, for fans of more modern fantasy adventures, D&D Icons could be for you. Could something futuristic like Halo or Horizon: Zero Dawn make sense for the D&D ruleset? Only time will tell, but it could open up the D&D experience to an even wider audience. Wizards has experimented with more modern content in the past, so it's not unprecedented.

Gundam Rogue Orbit Collector's Edition Like other special editions from Bandai Namco, Gundam Rogue Orbit combines a physical copy of the game with a few physical in-game goodies. It's the inclusion of a High-Grade model kit based on the new Gundam Helix mobile suit that could make this collector's edition sought after, as it will be exclusive to the game. Gundam model kits aren't usually hard to come by as Bandai Namco regularly keeps store shelves restocked with them, but the HG Helix model looks like a rare exception to that rule. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AiPllyLIvSo If you are planning to grab one, it's worth noting that HG Gundam model kits are 1/144-scale figures and are designed to appeal to casual builders with their moderate detail, minimal foil stickers, and durable design. You won't need too many tools to build one either, and the Helix design features a lot of panels and other mechanical details, so that could be a nice kit to build. The new trailer for the game also teased other shells that you can apply to the Helix to shake up its look, including an RX-78-2 skin and a red Zaku-inspired look that would make Char Aznable proud. Aside from the model, you'll also get a poster, reversible cover art, a pack of five promo cards, a steel case for the game disc, and DLC that includes 14 different color patterns for the Helix in the game. gamespot.com/articles/game-pass-is-getti.title: Game Pass Is Getting Worse, And More Expensive
gamespot.com/articles/game-pass-is-getti.excerpt: Microsoft has made a big announcement about one of the big perks of Xbox Game Pass, cloud streaming, and the news is not great. Starting in November, Microsoft will put limits on how many hours per month people can use the service, and then allow people to pay more to unlock more time. Below is a breakdown of how many hours you'll get included with the tier of Game Pass you're subscribed to: Game Pass Ultimate: 15 hours Game Pass Premium: 10 hours Game Pass Essential: 5 hours Microsoft said it understands this is a "meaningful change," especially for those who use the cloud regularly for gaming. However, the company said it estimates that these changes will impact about 4% of Game Pass subscribers, though the company did not share any specifics on how it arrived at that projection. A first look at the "cloud playtime remaining" UI on Xbox. For people who want or need more monthly streaming hours, Microsoft will allow people to buy more--but pricing was not announced. Additionally, Microsoft said that in November, for the first time, people will not need to have an Xbox Game Pass membership to stream games with the cloud. People outside of Game Pass will be able to buy cloud playtime through the Xbox Store, though, again, pricing was not shared. Microsoft said this option is meant to appeal to people who don't want to subscribe to a recurring membership like Game Pass and only want "occasional access." "We’re introducing this model because the cost of providing cloud gaming grows as more people use it and play for longer. Moving to monthly limits allows us to keep offering the service while continuing to invest in its reliability and performance. We understand that for some players the practical result is a higher cost," Microsoft said. The company added that it will "listen closely" to player feedback and make adjustments if necessary. gamespot.com/articles/the-metroidvania-i.title: The Metroidvania Is Decades Old, But One Year In Particular Is The Undisputed King
gamespot.com/articles/the-metroidvania-i.excerpt: The original Metroid and Castlevania both turn 40 years old this fall. As the two series most responsible for creating the “metroidvania,” we’re taking this occasion to take a comprehensive view of the popular genre. This is Metroidvania Week . Metroidvanias have been around for decades, with numerous high points over those years. Super Metroid–which set the template for the beloved (and much-iterated-upon) formula–hit the SNES in 1994. Castlevania: Symphony of the Night–which established a bold, non-linear direction for the series and helped pioneer the genre–followed in 1997. Metroid Prime–which proved this kind of game could work in 3D–touched down on the GameCube in 2002. And Hollow Knight: Silksong–which put metroidvanias at the center of gaming culture for one of the only times in their history–hit in late 2025. Though all of those titles have been and will be beacons for developers who came after, they were lonely lights. There were no other games released in 1994 that could join forces with Super Metroid; nothing to help Symphony of the Night make like its famous castle and turn the gaming world upside down. When metroidvanias had a moment in 2002, it was entirely driven by the Metroid series itself, as the GBA title Metroid Fusion launched the same day as Prime. Metroid Prime Remastered That wasn't the case in 2018, the best year in the genre's history. It was a year that stretched the boundaries of what a metroidvania could look like and play like, and how it could be built. There were original outings, new games in established series, and one very important port that brought a modern classic to a wider audience. The year's metroidvanias took inspiration from other genres (souls-likes, roguelikes, character action) and even mediums (pinball). Not all of these games worked, critically or commercially, but the overwhelming variety on display made it the best and easiest time ever for new players to try the genre out. gamespot.com/articles/dd-says-universes-.title: D&D Says Universes Beyond Is Designed To Bring In New Players, Not Push Out Existing Fans
gamespot.com/articles/dd-says-universes-.excerpt: Universes Beyond has been a major hit for Wizards of the Coast (WotC), as drawing outside intellectual properties like Final Fantasy into Magic: The Gathering and Dungeons & Dragons has brought new audiences to those tabletop experiences. But what about the core games that serve as a foundation for Universes Beyond? There is some concern amongst the fandom that Universes Beyond could delay or replace original core D&D rulebooks and campaigns, but WotC says that the classic side of the franchise is still its top priority. "A lot of the goal for it on our side was those new audiences," head of Dungeons & Dragons Dan Ayoub said to GameSpot's Jessica Cogswell at Gen Con. "There is certainly the fandom of, 'Oh cool, I want to play in Azeroth.' There is absolutely that layer. But a lot of things we want to do—and one thing that I am really passionate about—is bringing new players in. Role-playing games have been a huge part of my life, to my benefit. How do you ease that movement for people? It helps when people say, 'I know Azeroth,' or, 'I know Star Wars,' making it a little easier to get into it." https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sZWVrugrxJ8 Ayoub added that third-party crossovers are designed to bring new players into the hobby without taking away from what existing fans love. And if you're not a fan of seeing Doctor Who or Warhammer 40,000 in Magic: The Gathering? It's not like it's a vital part of the game that you have to buy to keep up with the meta. "The biggest difference from the Magic example is you do not need it," Ayoub explained. "You do not have to play it. I think of it as a line, just like Forgotten Realms is a line, and core D&D is a line. Something I say a lot—and certainly as we have been doing all of this work this year to move to this new dawn of D&D—is we cannot make every release be for everyone. It is impossible. Other unexpected additions coming to the paid expansion include Assassin’s Creed -esque naval combat, giant underwater dragons, and a new narrative threat that seemingly revolves around an unexplored location far beyond the Crimson Desert. Players can likely expect a new region dominated by a huge body of water, and a city in which abused workers are beginning to rebel against their leaders. Nothing about it makes sense, but players have come to expect that from Crimson Desert by now. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1fQCPmH6kOg But one of the most exciting things coming to the game as part of Charting the Unknown is the ability to construct your own buildings and fill them with whatever you like. The trailer is focused primarily on erecting what appears to be a massive castle outside the city, showcasing its evolution from a foundation in the ground to a formidable stone fortress. Available as a membership perk for Mega and Ultimate Fan subscribers, the Game Vault will now offer more than 100 games free of ads and in-app purchases, with new arrivals like Baki Hanma: Blood Arena and ReStory: Chill Electronics Repairs being added to the service. For fans of cozy experiences, ReStory is a delightful game where you run an electronics workshop and spend the day restoring old tech to working order while listening to some chill lofi beats. Designed to be satisfying and relaxing, it's a nostalgic look back at retro gaming hardware, cellphones, and other essential gadgets. Other upcoming games being added to Crunchyroll's vault include the stylish psychological-horror adventure Little Goody Two Shoes, the elegantly designed adventure Snufkin: Melody of Moominvalley, and Shovel Knight Pocket Dungeon, which reimagines the spade-wielding hero's quest as a roguelike with puzzle elements. Rounding out the arrivals is Streets of Rage 4 , which is still one of the best beat-'em-ups ever made. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XiYNNGR4uLo Crunchyroll also added a few more games recently, like the 2D brawler Baki Hanma: Blood Arena, a monster-hunting adventure where you cook what you catch in Battle Chef Brigade, and Beyblade X Xone for fans of the blade-spinning anime and toy franchise. If you're unfamiliar with it, the Crunchyroll Game Vault offers a curated library of premium mobile, indie, and anime-inspired games on iOS and Android devices. Available at no extra charge to Mega and Ultimate Fan members, this means that you're getting dozens of games on top of access to all the anime series and films through the streaming platform. gamespot.com/articles/the-witcher-4-will.title: The Witcher 4 Will Be Made “Predominantly Using People” And Not AI
gamespot.com/articles/the-witcher-4-will.excerpt: CD Projekt joint-CEO Michał Nowakowski has commented on how the studio thinks about artificial intelligence when it comes to developing games. Speaking during CD Projekt's latest earnings briefing, the executive said AI is "definitely becoming a thing in games development." However, he stressed that the Polish developer is still "predominantly using people" to make games. "AI, if anything, is a tool like many others that's helping in places that can maybe become more helpful in the future but we're not planning to rely on AI making complete games," he said, as reported by PC Gamer . https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=54dabgZJ5YA&rco=1 Nowakowski said CD Projekt makes "very complex games," and using AI would not be "the right or ethical path to follow." At the same time, Nowakowski said every studio--or at least its management--will decide for itself how it wants to use, or not use, AI. "So whether this is true for the whole industry, I'm not the person to make those statements. I think everybody has to make those judgments on their own," he said. The Witcher 4 is set for release in 2028 , and it kicks off a new trilogy of games. CD Projekt is also working on Cyberpunk 2 and a multiplayer Witcher game .

gamespot.com/articles/everything-from-th.title: Everything From The State Of Play That You Can Try Right Now
gamespot.com/articles/everything-from-th.excerpt: The most exciting part of a video game showcase is when developers shadow-drop something immediately after announcing it. Today's State of Play had a few such announcements. Demos for a new Final Fantasy game and anime-inspired action titles, as well as a port of a Double Fine game that was previously Xbox exclusive, are out now. Final Fantasy Resonance Demo https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IZvZYwQdXN8&pp=0gcJCRoMAYcqIYzv Final Fantasy Resonance is an HD-2D game based on the narrative of Brave Exvius, a game previously only available on mobile. This demo will give you a taste of the game's first chapter and all of the throwback pixel art and Final Fantasy character summons that come during that. Progression will carry over to the full game too, which is out on October 22. Although only the PS5 version was mentioned during the stream, the demo is also out now on PC, Switch, Switch 2, and Xbox Series X|S. Keeper's PS5 Port https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PilyJu1DDEo Keeper was released by Double Fine in October 2025 and is the latest title from Headlander and Stacking designer Lee Petty. It's a surreal, visually stunning game where you explore a decrepit world as a lighthouse and its fantastical bird companion. It flew under the radar last year, so it's great to see it come to PS5 now that Double Fine is independent once again. It got a price drop and new psychedelic mode today too. Stupid Never Dies Demo https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=k_33MQFuVEY Stupid Never Dies is a quirky new action game from Hiroyuki Kobayashi, a producer best known for his work on series like Dino Crisis and Dragon's Dogma at Capcom. You can get a taste of its flashy action from this new demo, which lasts two hours and lets you transfer progress once Stupid Never Dies launches on October 21. SlashZero Demo https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nrJuL3XSLTc SlashZero is a fast-paced action roguelike with an anime aesthetic where players control a time hacker trying to kill something called "Hieros-I."

gamespot.com/articles/double-fine-flexes.title: Double Fine Flexes Its Independence With Price Cuts And A New PS5 Release
gamespot.com/articles/double-fine-flexes.excerpt: After its liberation from Microsoft's ownership , the newly independent Double Fine Productions has been quite busy. At the September 2026 State of Play , PlayStation revealed that Double Fine's surreal adventure Keeper is shadow-dropping on PS5, and the studio added that the acclaimed game is getting some intriguing updates. Along with the surprise PS5 release, Keeper is also getting a "Psychedelic Mode," which is probably exactly what it sounds like. Considering how much bizarre imagery is already in the game, an even more "wild new way" to play the game should be a treat. And Double Fine wants to sweeten the deal with a price cut, which the studio implemented with its other recent title, Kiln. https://bsky.app/profile/doublefine.com/post/3mummzhp4ws2f Keeper launched in 2025 at a $30 price point and now sells for $20. Kiln, which released earlier in 2026, cost $20 for the base game, with a $30 deluxe "Fired Up" edition; those are now $8 and $10 , respectively. Unlike Keeper, Kiln launched on PS5 along with Xbox and Steam. Meanwhile, Double Fine revived its Amnesia Fortnight game jam and already exceeded its crowdfunding goal of $400,000 for the project. The game jam, a tradition for Double Fine since 2007 (and was halted while it was under Xbox's ownership), will result in the studio's next title. But the loftiest stretch goal in the crowdfunding campaign is the promise of a Brutal Legend 2 should it reach $100 million . It's a huge ask, and one that likely won't be met pending intervention from any moguls who are big Jack Black fans. Keeper was beloved by critics, with GameSpot's Keeper review calling it a "visual feast." Since Double Fine's spin-off from Xbox, purchases of its games will directly support the studio . The split from Microsoft occurred in July, but the studio unfortunately cut 25% of its staff as a result.

gamespot.com/articles/maneater-2-looks-l.title: Maneater 2 Looks Like A Dang Hoot (FYI, The Shark Can Wallrun Now)
gamespot.com/articles/maneater-2-looks-l.excerpt: We've come to expect a certain caliber of game from Sony State of Play: high production value, high artistic value. The trailers ran the gamut from Wolverine to a major expansion for Ghost of Yotei to an extended look at Final Fantasy 7 Resonance. All of these games look serious and expensive and artistic . They're the types of games for us Serious Gamers (™) who play Serious Games (™). Even the surprise appearance of Double Fine's Keeper is a showcase of a beautiful and artistically ambitious game. That may be why seeing Maneater 2, an action-RPG where you play as an angry and vengeful shark, felt so refreshing. The first Maneater was a silly concept that managed to squeeze out more depth than I expected. As a baby shark, you see your mother brutally killed by a reality-TV shark hunter named Scaly Pete, so you devote your whole shark life to growing bigger and stronger. It's an old-school revenge fantasy with a twist--that twist being that the entire game takes place underwater, because you're a shark. So the game loop was simplistic but enjoyable: Chomp down on increasingly dangerous and larger predators to gain valuable proteins and fats and grow bigger, as well as occasionally find mutagenics that help you gain special super-shark abilities. By the end of the game, you're a hulking monstrosity of a mega-shark, with abilities like bone armor plating or bioelectric shocks. And the whole thing is presented with a lighthearted touch, thanks in part to a performance by the great Chris Parnell as the narrator of an exploitive shark reality show. No one does an authoritative comedy voice like Dr. Spaceman . https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3GLGzZHzzQE Maneater 2 appears to understand what made the first one such a cult classic. According to the announcement from Tripwire, this one will take place at a five-star luxury resort called Neptune's Kingdom, giving you plenty of opportunities to chow down on hapless tourists. rockpapershotgun.com/onimusha-way-of-the.title: Onimusha: Way of the Sword is best when it's silly, and despite some gloomy open world slogging, sometimes even remembers it
rockpapershotgun.com/onimusha-way-of-the.excerpt: The opening minutes of Onimusha: Way of the Sword are glorious, in the sense that they’re utterly shambolic. Wandering ronin Musashi wakes up under a bridge, belts a wrong-footingly British "WOT?!" at some starving urchins eyeing up his rice ball, then proceeds to be chased around a muddy village by what feels like two thousand martial arts students, only occasionally stopping to boot a wooden plank into their faces or scoop up an imperilled dog. It’s goofy and brash and genuinely funny, in a way that immediately looks to elevate it among the field of po-faced fantasy slashers as effectively as any well-honed parry mechanic. Why in the following hours, then, does Way of the Sword make only occasional attempts to match this intro’s energy? Read more

gamespot.com/articles/gta-6-how-to-steal.title: GTA 6 Is Completely Changing How You Steal Cars
gamespot.com/articles/gta-6-how-to-steal.excerpt: Carjacking in Grand Theft Auto games has been, as the title denotes, a staple of the series. Up until now, it's largely been the same. While there have been more details and animations added over the years, the premise has remained that you'll walk up to a car, press Y or Triangle, throw the driver out, get in and drive away. If the car was parked, you'd execute the same button press to smash the window and steal it. With GTA 6 , carjacking is getting a complete overhaul. Here, we've got all of the information we know so far on how to steal cars in GTA 6. There are two ways to steal a car: taking one that's stationary, or taking one that someone's driving around in. However, there are more details that make GTA 6 feel more like true simulation gameplay now. How to steal a parked car As we saw in the GTA 6 extended look gameplay, when Jason approached a car, he had multiple options to choose from. The first option is a slim jim--a classic tool used to break into older vehicles. It slides down the window frame to adjust the lock, and in GTA 6, it seems like this is done via a lockpicking minigame. However, based on what we've heard so far, that won't work for every car. Depending on the year and model of the vehicle, you might not be able to use a slim jim. However, newer and more expensive cars might not work with this method. On top of that, there are trackers, meaning that the police can track your location when you steal a car. This changes the whole carjacking aspect of Grand Theft Auto. Normally, if you'd steal a car, you might catch some heat; maybe a nearby police officer sees you and follows you, but it's pretty easy to get away cleanly. This time, that isn't the case. If you do want to get away cleanly, you need an item to disable the tracking device. It seems like that item, along with the slim jim, is not something you start out with, meaning you'll need to progress through the story or complete side objectives to obtain them. gamespot.com/articles/im-begging-you-to-.title: I’m Begging You To Stop Obsessing Over Player Numbers And Just Enjoy Games
gamespot.com/articles/im-begging-you-to-.excerpt: Horror fans are confused. Every time a licensed multiplayer horror game gets brought up, two things tend to happen: commenters wonder if it can dethrone Dead by Daylight, and they speculate that the game will shut down quickly. It's happening again today, as I've recently published my Halloween review . Comments on YouTube and in Discord servers are already repeating the sentiments I've seen for many years now. "Probably be dead in six months to a year because no one can live aside DBD." "It will be dead within a month like the rest." "The real question is, will it go the way of Evil Dead, Friday the 13th, and Texas Chain Saw, and not touch Dead by Daylight?" I view this response as a kind of mass hallucination. This obsession over a game's health and future prospects is a widespread problem in a number of genres right now, but it's been especially irksome in the multiplayer horror space, where people rely on points that may feel true but don't prove accurate upon closer inspection. I've played nearly every licensed multiplayer horror game, like those named above and others, like Killer Klowns and Predator: Hunting Grounds. For the past decade, Hollywood licensors have been increasingly interested in adapting their intellectual properties to games , and with each new one revealed, there's an expectation among players and onlookers that they will die off, failing to topple the titan of the genre, Dead by Daylight. It's true that Dead by Daylight remains in a league of its own in terms of its community size. What I find absurd, though, is that these other games are seeking to usurp Behaviour Interactive's decade-long success story. Not one of these games seems to have aspirations or expectations of replacing DBD. Ultimately, they're very different things, and these other adaptations are only looking to earn their place alongside DBD. GTA 6 is itself inspired by Miami, so yes, this is one of those "simulation colonising reality" situations. The proposed publicity event would include "an immersive arrival experience" at Miami International Airport. with signs for Vice City and planes coated in GTA 6 livery, together with branded Metromover skytrains and specially designed manhole covers. It's a predictable bid to snaffle a few of those GTA marketing dollars, while driving up the regional circulation of affluent Vice City nuts. Also predictable: a few people, and specifically the cops, find the idea of their neighbourhood being mocked up to resemble a Grand Theft Auto game problematic. Miami-Dade sheriff Rosie Cordero-Stutz and commissioner Juan Carlos Bermudez have already spoken out against the potential deal, observing in a joint statement that "we should be promoting the Miami-Dade we have worked so hard to build, not a fictional version of our community defined by crime and violence.” Read more

gamespot.com/articles/moonlighter-2-feel.title: Moonlighter 2 Feels Like An Entirely Different Game, For Better And Worse
gamespot.com/articles/moonlighter-2-feel.excerpt: In a sea of Legend of Zelda homages, 2018's Moonlighter stood out with its lovely art style and a cool hook: What if the loot you gather on your dungeon-delving adventures wasn't just power-ups, but the wares you sell as part of your day job? Following Moonlighter's release, a number of smaller games, like Cult of the Lamb and Dave the Diver, have found success in complementing action mechanics with light management elements, so it's clearly a combo that works. It would have been easy for developer Digital Sun to simply give us a shinier, more polished version of that original concept in a sequel. Instead, Moonlighter 2: The Endless Vault, which has just released in version 1.0 after an early access period, surprisingly rethinks what a Moonlighter game is at its very core. That makes it comfortably live alongside the original, offering an experience that's distinct enough to enjoy both--or to come to the series anew without feeling lost. The visual differences between the first game and Moonlighter 2 are the most readily apparent changes. While characters like your shopkeeper, Will, are perfectly recognizable, they're rendered in a new 3D style with an isometric camera angle. That's already a huge change from the original, which was modeled after top-down Zelda games. Instead of procedurally-generated dungeons, you work your way through isometric roguelike stages with randomized assortments of enemies, building your strength as you go. You can imbue your attacks with effects like Poison and Hex to ramp up for the increasing challenges, or take your chances with a riskier build that relies on taking advantage of environmental hazards like Spikes. Moonlighter 2's Endless Vault is a an ominous glowing cube at the center of town Those elements make Moonlighter 2 feel more like a ground-up remake than a sequel. Internally, I groaned. I'm generally someone who can look past talking animals in a fantasy setting, but I draw the line at sci-fi. According to Robertson and Karpshyn, Exodus isn't just science fiction--it's hard science fiction, and its world follows the laws of physics and nature. Humanity cannot travel faster than the speed of light, they cannot traverse low-gravity environments without magboots, and yet, somehow, I'm supposed to believe that the game's protagonist, Jun Aslan, can communicate with certain animals. I'm also not supposed to find it painfully corny when he does so, or the animals talk back. For me, that's a pretty tall order. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zqhWyPq5lcM So no one was more surprised than I was when, at the end of the preview's two-hour playtime, I found myself locked in a genuinely gripping boss fight with an enormous, talking grizzly bear--a task I only took on in the first place due to the fact that I had recently become very emotionally attached to a clan of talking frogs. But we'll get back to Exodus's talking fauna in a minute, because the unhinged bear fight at the end of the level certainly wasn't the only aspect of the game that had me transfixed. What drew me in first was the story itself. In Exodus, players step into the shoes of the aforementioned Jun Aslan, a resident of the planet Lidon. Speaking to GameSpot's Jessica Cogswell at Gen Con, Manganiello explained how he wants D&D Icons to continue the legacy of the game's co-creator, Gary Gygax. "I was asked one year ago today by [Head of Dungeons & Dragons] Dan Ayoub, 'What would you do if you had...' I brought up the possibility of there being this line within D&D, and he said, 'Okay, who would you want to work with?' I said, 'Margaret [Weis] and Tracy [Hickman] to re-establish Dragonlance would be number one.' The idea that Gary Gygax got pushed out of the world that he created back in 1985 never sat right with me, and always made me sad," Manganiello said, referring to how Gygax was ousted from his company, Tactical Studies Rules Inc., in the '80s. https://youtu.be/3xd5WVr_Ihc "Even with the 3rd Edition, he and Dave Arneson were brought out on stage, and they really weren't allowed back in to re-establish their worlds or any of the work that they did. I know that Luke [Gygax] had just acquired a lot of Castle Greyhawk maps and unpublished maps from his father. I know that his father had wished that Luke would be able to continue his work after he passed away, and Luke was about to publish them all independently. I thought, 'What a great opportunity to pay respect to Gary as the Stan Lee of role-playing.' I am about appeasing ancestors or ghosts. Even after they're gone, I feel like they still hang around. I thought that there would be a lot of people who would be welcomed back to the gaming table if Gary's work was continued by Luke." gamespot.com/articles/steam-has-generate.title: Steam Has Generated $15 Billion In Revenue So Far In 2026, And New Games Are A Big Part Of It
gamespot.com/articles/steam-has-generate.excerpt: As the platform that gets the lion's share of PC game sales, Steam naturally makes a lot of money every year from commissions, publishing fees, and more through its storefront. But how much cash has it made so far in 2026? Unsurprisingly, enough dough to buy Valve co-founder Gabe Newell a few more superyachts . According to the head of market analysis at Alinea Analytics, Rhys Elliot, Steam has made $15 billion in 2026, and with a massive period of high-profile game releases around the corner, that number is likely to surge even higher before the year is over. Steam's top releases by gross revenue include AAA games and breakout indie hits, with Forza Horizon 6 leading the charge. The new racing game earned Steam $210.5 million in revenue, while Crimson Desert sales were responsible for $203.3 million, Resident Evil Requiem made just over $200.9 million, and Slay the Spire 2 brought in over $148 million. Rounding out the list is Subnautica 2 at $139.2 million and Meccha Chameleon at $89.8 million. https://twitter.com/superhys/status/2095562045185822951 That's a lot of cheddar, but it only counts for 6.6% of the $15 billion that Steam has made so far. Elliot noted that the top 100 new games by gross revenue make up 15.9% of Steam's total 2026 revenue so far--around $2.4 billion. Crimson Desert is also doing a lot of heavy lifting, as it accounts for about 18% of all new-IP revenue in the top 100. "Of the new-game top 100, 63% were actually new IP, but 52.5% of the revenue ($1.25B) came from established IP," Elliot wrote. "But it’s worth noting Crimson Desert, with its $203M, accounts for about 18% of all new-IP revenue in the top 100. gamespot.com/articles/gta-6-online-could.title: GTA 6 Online Could Struggle To Pull Players Away From GTA Online, Says Valve Veteran
gamespot.com/articles/gta-6-online-could.excerpt: What's the biggest question about Grand Theft Auto 6 ? Easily Rockstar's plans for GTA Online, and how it'll factor into the post-launch plans of GTA 6. Considering just how consistently popular GTA Online has been for the developer, it is strange that Rockstar has yet to publicly comment on the anticipated multiplayer mode, as it has so far only focused on talking about the "single-player experience" of GTA 6. And that could be a major problem for the franchise. As Valve veteran Chet Faliszek pointed out, Rockstar might be caught between a rock and a hard place. GTA Online continues to be a big money-maker for Rockstar and its parent group, Take-Two Interactive, but moving people to a GTA 6 online mode is a challenging prospect. As Faliszek explained, a lot of GTA Online players are heavily invested in the game, and thanks to GTA 5 regularly going on sale--or being given away for free through various programs--access to it has been cheap and easy. "What are they going to do? That's a mess. We can all look through recent history--without pointing fingers--and see some people who did it by total replacement. We can see people who tried to win people over, and when that didn't happen, shut down the other thing," Faliszek said. https://www.youtube.com/embed/21mhuwI60Tk Rockstar and Take-Two would likely want to move people over to the new GTA Online as soon as possible, but forcing people to make a fresh start could be an uphill battle. As people have pointed out, major updates for GTA Online could slow as Rockstar instead focuses on GTA 6, which would be a slow death for the groundbreaking mode. Whatever choice Rockstar makes, it won't please everyone . There are a few approaches Rockstar could take--like making GTA 6 Online a separate experience that exists alongside GTA 5 Online--but there's no one-size-fits-all solution for this brewing problem. gamespot.com/articles/lets-stop-saying-m.title: Let’s Stop Saying “Metroidvania”
gamespot.com/articles/lets-stop-saying-m.excerpt: The original Metroid and Castlevania both turn 40 years old this fall. As the two series most responsible for creating the “metroidvania,” we’re taking this occasion to take a comprehensive view of the popular genre. This is Metroidvania Week . When we talk about something, we should talk about it in ways people can understand. You have to be deep in the "gamer" weeds to have any idea what "Metroidvania" means, though. You have to be familiar with not one but two different decades-old game series, and not just familiar with their names or generally aware of their existence, but knowledgeable about how they're designed and how they're actually played. And if you're that well-versed in Metroid and Castlevania, you know enough to know that neither truly invented this type of action game. And you know that the Castlevania games, the first of which didn't have any of the distinctive traits that define the genre that bears their name, didn't even popularize it, as Metroid did. (Yes, Vampire Killer and Simon's Quest both had Metroid-y elements, but the former wasn't open-ended enough and the latter was too open-ended and obtuse; it wasn't until Castlevania: Symphony of the Night, over a decade later, that Castlevania really jumped on board the 'Troid train.) Castlevania didn't adopt search-action mechanics until Symphony of the Night So either you have no idea what "Metroidvania" means, or you know that it's not even that accurate a term, and in either case, the solution is simple: Stop using it. I didn't have a lot of hard-and-fast rules during my 15 years editing the games section of a second-tier entertainment site that used to be a third-tier music magazine, but any of the dozens of writers who wrote for me knew of one big one: We tried as hard as possible to not use the word "metroidvania." gamespot.com/articles/some-of-the-best-m.title: Some Of The Best Metroidvanias Have Gone Criminally Overlooked
gamespot.com/articles/some-of-the-best-m.excerpt: The original Metroid and Castlevania both turn 40 years old this fall. As the two series most responsible for creating the “metroidvania,” we’re taking this occasion to take a comprehensive view of the popular genre. This is Metroidvania Week . Metroidvanias are very popular among indie developers, and small studios have produced some of the genre's finest examples. Just one look at Steam presents a dizzying array of search-action games, many of which you probably didn't know existed. Among all of these titles, however, there are a few that are special: They're made by Team Ladybug, a Japanese development group whose expertise in the genre is outstanding. While they've made games in other genres--like the excellent arcade shooter Drainus--Team Ladybug specializes in the metroidvania, and they are undisputed masters of their craft. Yet when I hear others wax on about great games in this genre, their works are rarely mentioned. I'd like to do something about that. I'm going to recommend you three of Team Ladybug's metroidvania masterpieces: Touhou Luna Nights, Record of Lodoss War: Deedlit in Wonder Labyrinth, and Blade Chimera. Touhou Luna Nights , first released in 2019 on PC and since released on Switch, PlayStation 4, and Xbox One, is a strong example of what makes Team Ladybug's games unique and enjoyable. Luna Nights is based on the mythos of the Touhou Project--a popular semi-collaborative setting inspired heavily by Japanese mythology that would require an article of its own to fully explain. Leading lady Sakuya Izayoi is a knife-wielding maid who serves the vampire sisters who reside in the Scarlet Devil Mansion. She's sent to a bizarre parallel dimension for reasons unknown--one that strips her of her unique time-manipulation powers. Sakuya needs to get her powers back, get out of this strange world, and figure out which of the Touhou universe's numerous troublemakers is responsible for everything. gamespot.com/articles/starcraft-return-a.excerpt: BlizzCon 2026 is right around the corner, and for Blizzard fans, there's an air of excitement as signs point to a dormant franchise possibly being revived. StarCraft has been largely dormant since the release of StarCraft 2: Legacy of the Void in 2015--and a huge update in June--but could the sci-fi series be making a comeback? If recent rumors and other weird stuff are to be believed, we could be in for some sort of an announcement during the BlizzCon opening ceremony--and to paraphrase one grizzled space marine, hell, it's about time. Here's what we've heard and seen so far. Blizzard might not make the next StarCraft game If a new StarCraft game is in development, it looks like it might not be Blizzard working on it. According to a report from Korean newspaper Chosun (via ResetEra ), Korean gaming giant and Arc Raiders publisher Nexon is close to finalizing a deal to develop a StarCraft sequel, possibly StarCraft 3. This would be a huge deal, but it makes sense given how significant StarCraft is in Korean culture. The original real-time strategy game laid the groundwork for esports in that country, and it enjoyed years of popularity there. At the same time, Nexon has also been linked to rumors of a StarCraft shooter , which is reportedly set to be revealed at BlizzCon this month. In older reports, Bloomberg reporter Jason Schrierer mentioned in his 2024 book, Play Nice: The Rise, Fall, and Future of Blizzard Entertainment, that former Far Cry lead Dan Hay was spearheading a new StarCraft project , but he didn't divulge any other details. It wouldn't be the first time Blizzard has attempted to launch a StarCraft shooter; back in the mid-2000s, StarCraft: Ghost was poised to let players step into the boots of the infamous Terran black ops unit during the events of StarCraft’s Brood War expansion. gamespot.com/articles/10-tips-you-should.excerpt: Halloween: The Game is the latest asymmetrical horror game from IllFonic. It features the typical genre staples, including the familiar PvP-based loop--where players, acting as civilians, must escape a given location while being pursued by a player-controlled monster. Fans of the genre should know what to expect. What makes Halloween: The Game stand out, however, is in how it incorporates NPCs into the mix, as well as key elements from the popular slasher franchise. IllFonic has created a survival horror experience that mirrors its source material. Because of this, Halloween: The Game is more about stepping into a role than playing hide-and-seek with Michael Myers. Players controlling residents of Haddonfield will need to do more than just survive the night if they want to beat Myers. At the same time, Myers doesn't have to kill every human-controlled citizen to win. Whichever side leans most into its respective role will usually come out on top. In order to help players do just that, we've gathered a few helpful tips that detail some of the nuances found in each role. Note: These tips are based on a pre-released version of Halloween: The Game. While most of them still should hold true post-launch, some might change slightly after a few patches. gamespot.com/articles/game-director-fina.title: Game Director Finally Addresses His Rumored Foot Fetish–Wait, Not Kojima, The Other One
gamespot.com/articles/game-director-fina.excerpt: A prolific Japanese game developer has finally addressed all that weird foot imagery in his video games. What? No, I'm not talking about Hideo Kojima (he's busy hanging out with The Backrooms director right now, anyway). I'm referring to Dark Souls and Elden Ring director Hidetaka Miyazaki, who has finally addressed online speculation that he is a foot guy. “It's not necessarily something I’m consistently aware of--maybe it’s something subconscious coming through,” Miyazaki told The Guardian in response to a question about all the hand imagery in his upcoming action-RPG, The Duskbloods . "Take a look online and there’s a rumor that I have a bit of a thing for feet, but I’m not honestly sure where this comes from." Seriously, stop making it weird. Though Miyazaki says he's not sure where the idea that he has a "thing for feet" comes from, it's something fans of his games have noticed for years . Whether we're talking The Maiden in Black from Demons' Souls or Priscilla (or Gwunevere, or Sister Friede, or Maneater Mildred) from Dark Souls, it's hard to ignore how many barefoot women are roaming Miyazaki's fictional worlds. Elden Ring's Malenia is rocking bare feet, too, although hers are metal prosthetics. The game's beaches even differentiate between barefoot players and those who are wearing footwear. So what's with all the shoeless women in Souls games? According to Miyazaki, it's about depicting the human experience. Or something. "I feel like I’m trying to depict some side of human nature or the human existence that is difficult to describe,” he elaborated. But regardless of what fans might think , Miyazaki insists this is not a Tarantino situation. And to be fair, plenty of other games are even more foot-focused than Miyazaki's work--and far less subtle about it.

gamespot.com/articles/stage-tour-is-more.excerpt: There are some games that you hope will demonstrate how much muscle memory can survive years of neglect. Hand me a plastic guitar, put a rhythm game in front of me, and apparently my brain still thinks it knows what it's doing. Having not touched a guitar controller since around 2009, when Guitar Hero 5 was released, my hands-on time with Stage Tour at Gamescom went a little differently than I'd hoped. Getting to grips with the new rhythm game from RedOctane Games, I opted for guitar, naturally. If you're going to spend time with a game that is openly positioning itself as a spiritual successor to the Guitar Hero and Rock Band franchises, it feels obligatory to pick up that instrument. Rather than making the spectacularly poor decision of attempting Expert difficulty and embarrassing myself, I settled on Medium, and was promptly reminded that remembering how rhythm games work and actually being good at them are two very different things. https://youtu.be/xU-qK6FyUoM The first few notes went pretty well, but things quickly began to unravel. "Here's my guitar solo," I announced, with considerably more confidence than my mediocre gameplay warranted. Fortunately, the developers behind Stage Tour were more forgiving than the note charts I was fumbling. "No bandmate left behind!" joked Jack Guinchard, global brand manager, "It's a rock tour; bad shit happens." A short while later, the song had finished, and my pitiful score flashed before me. Still, there's something immediately familiar about Stage Tour, and that's clearly intentional. RedOctane isn't pretending that its predecessors never existed, and it's not trying to reinvent the formula that made them so popular. gamespot.com/articles/xbox-new-tcl-partn.excerpt: Xbox has announced a new partnership with TCL, which will see the Xbox app added to "select" models from the brand. This means that owners of those TCL TVs won't need to spend $500 on an Xbox Series S or $800 on an Xbox Series X, as they can instead take advantage of the cloud-based gaming features offered as part of a monthly Xbox Game Pass subscription-- but only for a few hours per month , before they need to start coughing up some extra cash to buy more hours to play. If your TCL TV is supported, all you'll need is a Game Pass subscription and an Xbox controller to start playing. Xbox Game Pass also offers a library of games to play, so you'll be good to go once you're signed up and logged in. As a reminder, you'll only get a few hours of cloud streaming depending on which tier of Game Pass you sign up for. The cheapest option, Game Pass Essential, will give you five hours of cloud streaming; Game Pass Premium doubles that number to 10 hours, and Game Pass Ultimate caps out at 15 hours. Pricing for top-up cloud streaming packages has not yet been announced. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QN1JlrG2esw This announcement also comes during a busy time for Xbox, as its next big first-party game is Gears of War: E-Day. It arrives after a busy year for the gaming brand, which saw 75 day-one releases through its subscription program. More Game Pass titles are also on the way in Septembe r, with Speedrunners 2 and Call of Duty: Black Ops Cold War headlining the first wave of new arrivals. TCL TVs are typically positioned as budget-to-mid-range sets, which could potentially give Xbox exposure to millions of consumers who wouldn't normally buy one of their expensive consoles. The Azure servers that Xbox uses for streaming games belong to its parent company, Microsoft, and these have started to turn a tidy profit for the company. No, it’s fine. It’s fine . I’d like to say that the demo’s shooting and roleplaying moments made up for the lack of squidmates. In some places, particularly when venturing back out into the vacuum, it actually did. gamespot.com/reviews/nba-2k27-review.title: NBA 2K’s Best Mode Is Even Better This Year
gamespot.com/reviews/nba-2k27-review.excerpt: NBA 2K has long been the standard-bearer for high-quality sports games. It's the pinnacle that other series like Madden, FC, and even the oft-beloved MLB The Show aspire to emulate in whatever ways their respective sports allow. That's not to say it gets everything right, but it often feels like the team at Visual Concepts is competing against itself. It creates trends; it doesn't chase them. That's always been most obvious in The City, the series' social PvPvE hub and the lifeblood of the game's community. Though some other parts of the game are more uneven with this year's entry, The City proves that if you only plan to play one sports game this year, NBA 2K27 is the way to go. The City is where players can meet up for basketball games of varying sweat levels, buy cosmetics, and complete live-service challenges--it is the center of NBA 2K27's solar system. This hub is thoughtfully attached to the single-player MyCareer mode at the proverbial hip, and this pairing offers more enjoyable and immersive things to do as a tandem than most other sports games taken in their totality. This year, The City makes several smart changes. At the core of it all is the long-awaited ability to import custom women characters into the mode. Aesthetically, this is a nice change that lets the hub world better reflect real-life streetball communities--it's always been true that women have existed in these spaces in real life, so they should be included in NBA 2K, too. However, this positive change does come with a frustrating caveat: The MyCareer mode doesn't account for them, thereby siloing these women avatars into The City exclusively. Plus, this requires anyone who wants to run around in The City as a woman to create a second avatar as a man if they want to go into MyCareer's story mode. So as awesome as this all is to see, it also feels like a frustrating half-step forward. Finally bringing women avatars into The City makes for a more diverse and dynamic social space. New landmarks

gamespot.com/articles/before-hbos-the-la.title: Before HBO’s The Last Of Us, An Entirely Different Adaptation Was Proposed
gamespot.com/articles/before-hbos-the-la.excerpt: Naughty Dog's first effort to adapt The Last of Us for the screen was not as an HBO TV show, but a movie, a fact that recently began doing the rounds again on social media. Like with many Hollywood productions, The Last of Us had a tumultuous, long development period as a movie before it was ultimately abandoned in favor of what is now a hit series. While not everyone agrees with the creative departures from the source material for the TV series on HBO, it's undeniably a success and one of HBO's biggest hits lately. Let's look back at how The Last of Us originated as a movie and run through the key developments that led to it becoming a TV show. The original movie pitch People across X recently discovered a post from Sony Pictures in 2014 declaring that The Last of Us was "soon to be a major motion picture." This was a real, studio-sponsored image, not a fan mock-up. There was officially produced key art, showing Ellie wielding a knife. There was a "secret panel" at San Diego Comic-Con that year featuring director Sam Raimi, who was originally attached to produce the movie, having already had huge success at Sony with his Spider-Man films. https://twitter.com/sonypictures/status/492757891229552641?s=46 That The Last of Us was originally going to be a movie is not surprising given how many video game movies came before it and how many have been released since (with varying degrees of success). This was a year after The Last of Us came out in 2013. It was a hot property, as the game was a critical and a commercial success for Naughty Dog and Sony. With Sony also owning and operating its own film studio, all the synergies were there for Sony to make a Last of Us film. Neil Druckmann, who directed The Last of Us game, confirmed in 2014 that the movie would adapt the story of The Last of Us , as opposed to branching off in some other way.
